title: Spring warmth gave no clear common link to absolute butterfly-swallow sighting gaps in Japan in 1953-2020
abstract: We tested whether spring warmth was linked to a larger absolute gap between butterfly and swallow first sightings. We used 4077 paired records at 69 Japan stations in 1953-2020. Separate North and South models in two periods controlled station and report mode, January temperature and a time trend. Absolute-gap slopes were +0.988, -0.316, +0.667 and +0.396 days per C. All four corrected intervals included zero. A January-February check gave a positive corrected interval only in the later South. Other windows and controls did not show a clear common response. Exact delay bounds showed that separate sighting delays of up to two days permit both point-slope signs in all four samples. These bounds describe assumed error, not measured delay or sampling uncertainty. First sightings do not identify true event dates or full seasonal overlap. Selected records, coarse weather, uncertain effort and weather windows that extend beyond sightings limit inference. This secondary analysis reuses a published panel and is not independent data validation. Code, the attributed CC BY 4.0 input panel, source hashes, aggregate results and numerical checks support offline reproduction.

display.caption: Absolute-gap slopes with four-test intervals, and sharp independent sighting-delay bounds. Delay bounds are fixed-record possibilities, not confidence intervals.

citations.reason: Reuses its verified 4077-pair input, sample rules and weather fields. Adds absolute separation and sharp delay bounds; observations overlap fully.
Prior signed-gap delay sensitivity; our outcome is absolute separation.
